key_insight: Ultrasonic nanocrystal surface modification (UNSM) changed the hardness of Cr3C2–NiCr coatings in a strongly sample-dependent way, with detonation-sprayed samples showing a tighter hardness band than HVOF deposits.
engineering_relevance: For wear-resistant coating design, the results show that deposition route and UNSM settings can significantly influence local mechanical performance and should be tuned together rather than independently.
method: Compared detonation-sprayed (DS) and HVOF Cr3C2–NiCr coatings after UNSM
Tested 4 treated samples per deposition route at 20/30 N and 20/30 µm vibration amplitude
Measured instrumental hardness at 300 mN load and examined post-scratch SEM morphology
evidence_signal: Hardness ranged from 820–970 HV for DS coatings and 546–1165 HV for HVOF coatings, with SEM revealing heterogeneous contrast and crack-like features after scratch testing.
watch_item: The scratch morphology is qualitative and does not isolate UNSM-induced damage or provide a definitive ranking of scratch resistance.
paper_title: HARDNESS AND POST-SCRATCH SURFACE MORPHOLOGY OF Cr₃C₂–NiCr COATINGS AFTER ULTRASONIC NANOCRYSTAL SURFACE MODIFICATION
